text:
sam.w (Acme): Hey — since the midnight deploy our Private agents keep failing calls to api.redwood.com. Symptoms: intermittent 407 from proxy, sometimes TLS handshake failures (tls: handshake failure). Origin is our VPC egress through corporate proxy (BlueGate) with TLS inspection enabled. Can you advise?

ben.support: Thanks Sam — sorry about the outage. Quick checklist first: do you have any recent tcpdumps or curl traces? Can you run these from one of the affected Private hosts and paste results: 

1) direct TLS test (bypassing proxy if possible):
```
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.com:443 -servername api.redwood.com -brief
```

2) test via proxy with proxytunnel:
```
curl -v --proxy http://<proxy_host>:<port> --proxytunnel https://api.redwood.com/v1/health
```

3) verbose request showing proxy auth: 
```
curl -v --proxy http://<user>:<pass>@<proxy>:<port> https://api.redwood.com/v1/health
```

Also please capture the failing HTTP response headers from the host (include the full 407/502/504 body if present).

sam.w (Acme): I tried 2 & 3 — the proxytunnel command usually returns "HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established" then a TLS handshake, but on failures the TLS handshake immediately drops with "tls: handshake failure" and curl shows SSL peer certificate: certificate signed by unknown authority (because BlueGate intercepts). We also get plain 407s when our proxy credentials rotate. We do have transparent interception enabled; proxy is doing SSL inspection for some domains.

carmen-net: Two immediate red flags: 1) If the proxy is intercepting TLS and re-terminating connections (SSL termination + re-initiate), it will change the server certificate and might also rewrite the SNI/header or not pass through original SNI. Redwood endpoints rely on SNI for virtual-host routing in some infra; missing/altered SNI can cause the upstream TLS to land on the wrong cert/back-end and trigger 502s. 2) Some proxies rewrite or strip CONNECT semantics and inject their own headers which breaks long-lived streaming responses (chunked/transfer-encoding).

ben.support: Can you try to see which SNI the proxy sends upstream? On the host run tcpdump during a failing request and share a pcap (we need the TLS ClientHello). If you can’t share PCAPs publicly, please upload to our secure S3 and we’ll pull it. A quick local test you can run to inspect SNI (requires tcpdump + tshark):
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/redwood_fail.pcap host api.redwood.com and port 443
# reproduce the failure for ~10s then stop
# analyze locally: tshark -r /tmp/redwood_fail.pcap -Y "ssl.handshake.extensions_server_name" -V
```

deploy-bot: deployment job logs show repeated "upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header" and occasional 502 body: "upstream reset during TLS handshake".

carmen-net: Another repro trick — curl against the proxy but force a raw CONNECT to certify behavior:
```
# open a raw connection to the proxy and issue CONNECT manually:
printf 'CONNECT api.redwood.com:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.com\r\nProxy-Authorization: Basic <base64>\r\n\r\n' | nc <proxy_host> <proxy_port> -q 3
# If you get "HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established" then try to start TLS:
openssl s_client -connect <proxy_host>:<proxy_port> -servername api.redwood.com -starttls smtp
# (the above combo depends on your environment, but the idea is to see whether SNI is preserved)
```

ben.support: Common enterprise proxy misbehaviors we've seen: 
- SSL inspection that terminates TLS and re-establishes a new TLS session without preserving the original server_name (SNI)
- Rewriting Host or Path headers on the proxied connection (shouldn't happen on CONNECT tunnels)
- Stripping or rewriting Proxy-Authorization/Proxy-Connection headers, causing intermittent 407s
- Changing transfer encoding (removing chunked) which breaks streaming endpoints

If your proxy is doing ssl_bump/mitm, the recommended configuration is to add an explicit bypass (no proxy) for *.redwood.com or at minimum for api.redwood.com so the CONNECT is a pure passthrough. For Squid example: add an acl and bypass rule: 
```
# squid.conf snippet
acl redwood dstdomain .api.redwood.com
always_direct allow redwood
ssl_bump allow redwood
```

sam.w (Acme): We can't bypass for all users due to compliance, but we can add a carve-out for service accounts/nodes in that VPC. Is there a way to make Redwood tolerable to interception?

carmen-net: If interception is mandatory, two things to validate: 1) Proxy must present a cert that your hosts trust (install proxy CA into the host truststore) so the client does not reject intercepted certs. 2) Proxy must preserve SNI; if it doesn't, you will see the wrong cert or routing failures. If the proxy replaces SNI we sometimes see consistent upstream failures.

ben.support: Also check that the proxy allows CONNECT to port 443 and 80 for api.redwood.com. Some policies only allow CONNECT to 443 but block higher ports used by alternate endpoints. Also check proxies that require TLS1.2+ — older clients fall back and fail the handshake.

sam.w (Acme): Action items we can do now:
- Run tcpdump on host and upload pcap (we'll attach to ticket)
- Paste full curl -v output (we'll redact creds)
- Check proxy config for ssl_bump / intercept rules for api.redwood.com and add an allowlist for service nodes

ben.support: We'll escalate to eng-infra and our Private infra team. Please attach the pcap + curl logs to this thread. In parallel, if you can temporarily route those hosts' egress via a NAT without BlueGate (even for a small subset) that will validate whether the proxy is the cause. If that fixes it, then the fix is a proxy carve-out.

eng-infra-oncall: Looping in infra — can you upload the pcap to the secure bucket and drop the path here? Also please capture the proxy access logs for the timeframe (we want the CONNECT entry + any ssl_bump logs). If you prefer, we can take a redacted snapshot.

sam.w (Acme): Uploaded pcap to our S3 at s3://acme-uploads/redwood/1769802456.pcap (IAM link shared). Attached curl traces as `redwood_curl_1769802456.txt`.

ben.support: Received — thanks. Initial look: the ClientHello in the pcap shows SNI present from the host, but the proxy's re-originated ClientHello upstream uses SNI "bluegate.local" (proxy default) — that explains the mismatch. We recommend either:
- Configure BlueGate to preserve the requested SNI for upstream connections, or
- Add an allowlist so the proxy does not intercept traffic to api.redwood.com for those nodes.

carmen-net: For completeness, check whether your Private deployment is validating the leaf certificate chain or doing certificate pinning. If you have pinning and the proxy replaces certs, clients will fail. Also ensure that the proxy isn't removing the `TE: trailers` header (breaks chunked streaming).

ben.support: I'm marking this as a critical P1 for support -> eng-infra. Next steps: eng-infra to review proxy config and either add carve-out or update ssl_bump rules. Sam — once infra confirms changes, please re-run the curl proxytunnel test and drop the new pcap. :eyes:

sam.w (Acme): Will do, thanks all. Appreciate quick turnaround. :pray:
